metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with a deployable JAX-WS endpoint (PurchaseOrderService.java with @WebService annotation) and database writes present. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Service owns persistent state (Oracle 11g database via JDBC), exposes a write endpoint (INSERT into partner_orders), and manages entity lifecycle. Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.18 falls in the Not Ready band (< 1.5), but 11 High findings yield Remediation Required tier (2-11 High rule). The pervasive Score-1 findings drive the very low overall score while the core-question count (11) falls just within the Remediation Required boundary rather than reaching the >=12 threshold for Not Ready.

findings.title: All compute on unsupported JBoss AS 5.1 / RHEL 6 — no managed services
findings.description: All compute runs on a bare RHEL 6 VM with JBoss AS 5.1. No managed container orchestration or serverless in use.
findings.gap: No managed compute at all. Entire runtime on unsupported OS and application server.
findings.recommendation: Containerize the application and deploy on ECS/Fargate or EKS. Migrate from Java 6 to Java 17+ with a modern application server.

findings.title: Self-managed Oracle 11g database — no managed database service
findings.description: Oracle 11g accessed via hardcoded JDBC connection to internal IP. Database is entirely self-managed.
findings.gap: Database is self-managed with no automated failover, backups, or scaling. Oracle 11g is past EOL.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL using AWS DMS.

findings.title: No workflow orchestration — all logic hardcoded in single method
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. Single operation entirely hardcoded with no retry or error handling strategy.
findings.gap: All processing logic in a single try/catch block with no structured error handling or retry.
findings.recommendation: Focus on structured error handling and retry logic. Consider Step Functions if service grows to multi-step operations.

findings.title: No messaging infrastructure — state changes not propagated
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. Purchase order state changes are not propagated via events.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Downstream systems must poll the database.
findings.recommendation: Introduce SQS or EventBridge to publish order creation events for downstream consumption.

findings.title: No network security — service exposed over plain HTTP with no isolation
findings.description: No VPC, security groups, or network segmentation. Service exposed over unencrypted HTTP.
findings.gap: Service exposed over unencrypted HTTP with no network isolation. Database accessed via raw IP.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a VPC with private subnets. Place behind ALB/API Gateway with TLS. Restrict DB access via security groups.

findings.title: No API gateway or load balancer — direct service exposure
findings.description: Service exposed directly at hardcoded address with no gateway, ALB, or throttling.
findings.gap: No managed entry point. Partners connect directly to the application server.
findings.recommendation: Place an API Gateway or ALB in front of the service with throttling, auth, and request validation.

findings.title: No auto-scaling — static single-instance deployment
findings.description: No auto-scaling mechanisms. Single JBoss instance on a single VM with static capacity.
findings.gap: No ability to respond to traffic spikes or scale down. Single instance with no horizontal scaling.
findings.recommendation: After containerization, configure ECS service auto-scaling or EKS HPA.

findings.title: No backup or recovery configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration found. Oracle 11g database has no defined backup retention or restore procedures.
findings.gap: No automated backups, no restore testing, no recovery point objective defined.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS/Aurora for automated backups. Until then, implement Oracle RMAN backup schedules.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code — all manual provisioning
findings.description: No IaC files exist. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or any infrastructure definition. All infrastructure is manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. Infrastructure changes are non-reproducible and not version-controlled.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in CDK or Terraform: VPC, compute, database, load balancer, security groups.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation — all deployments manual
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Build uses Ant with manual wsgen/wsimport. No build file even present in repository.
findings.gap: All builds and deployments entirely manual. No automated quality gates.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD with CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions with automated test, build, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Java 6 with deprecated JAX-WS RPC/encoded — compound legacy
findings.description: Java 6 (EOL 2013) with JAX-WS RPC/encoded style on JBoss AS 5.1 (EOL). Both language version and framework are deeply regressed.
findings.gap: Compound legacy: Java 6, JAX-WS RPC/encoded, JBoss AS 5.1. Requires language + framework + server modernization.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Java 17+ with Spring Boot 3.x or Quarkus. Replace JAX-WS with REST/OpenAPI or Spring WS.

findings.title: Tightly-coupled single-class monolith with no module boundaries
findings.description: Single Java class containing all logic: XML parsing, database connectivity, SQL execution, error handling. No separation of concerns.
findings.gap: No module boundaries, no layering, pervasive shared state. Cannot scale or deploy subsystems independently.
findings.recommendation: Refactor into layered architecture: API layer, service layer, data access layer. See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: All communication synchronous — no async patterns
findings.description: Entirely synchronous SOAP/HTTP. No async patterns, no event emission, no message publishing.
findings.gap: No async communication for cross-service state propagation. Order creation events not published.
findings.recommendation: Publish order creation events to SQS/EventBridge while maintaining synchronous partner response.

findings.title: No timeout or async handling for potentially slow operations
findings.description: All operations synchronous with no timeout handling, no connection pooling, no protection against slow DB responses.
findings.gap: No timeout management. Database operations can block indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Implement connection pooling with timeout configuration. Add async job patterns for future growth.

findings.title: No API versioning — breaking changes affect all consumers
findings.description: No versioning strategy. Single SOAP namespace with no version identifier. WSDL drifts from implementation.
findings.gap: No versioning mechanism. Any contract change breaks all partners simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Introduce versioned namespaces for SOAP or URL-path versioning for REST migration.

findings.title: All endpoints hardcoded — no service discovery
findings.description: Database connection uses hardcoded IP. WSDL exposes hardcoded hostname. No dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: Hardcoded endpoints create deployment coupling. Moving DB or service requires code changes.
findings.recommendation: Externalize endpoints to environment variables or configuration service. Use AWS Service Discovery.

findings.title: Purchase order XML not stored in managed object storage
findings.description: Incoming PO XML is parsed in memory and discarded. Original documents are not persisted in S3 or any managed store.
findings.gap: Unstructured data (PO XML) not stored. No document retention, no audit trail, no reprocessing capability.
findings.recommendation: Store incoming PO XML in S3 with lifecycle policies. Enable versioning for audit trails.

findings.title: No data access layer — raw JDBC inline with business logic
findings.description: DriverManager.getConnection() with raw Statement.executeUpdate() and string-concatenated SQL directly in the service method.
findings.gap: No data access abstraction. Database queries inline with business logic. SQL injection vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Introduce repository pattern with connection pool (HikariCP) and parameterized queries.

findings.title: Oracle 11g past end-of-life — no version management
findings.description: Oracle 11g referenced in README and JDBC driver. Extended Support ended December 2020. No version pinning in configuration.
findings.gap: Database engine past EOL. No security patches, no vendor support, no version management strategy.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL using AWS DMS and SCT.

findings.title: No encryption at rest for partner financial data
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. Oracle 11g stores partner purchase order data without encryption. No KMS configuration.
findings.gap: Partner financial data stored in plaintext. No encryption at rest.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS/Aurora with encryption enabled (KMS customer-managed key).

findings.title: WS-Security plaintext password over HTTP — no token-based auth
findings.description: Authentication uses WS-Security PasswordText over plain HTTP. No OAuth2, JWT, or modern token-based auth.
findings.gap: Credentials transmitted in cleartext. No modern authentication mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT-based authentication. Use Cognito or API Gateway authorizers.

findings.title: No centralized identity provider — self-managed flat-file credentials
findings.description: Partner credentials stored in flat properties file. No federation, no SSO, no external IdP integration.
findings.gap: Self-managed authentication with no audit trail, rotation, or federation.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito for partner identity management with client credentials flow.

findings.title: Hardcoded database credentials in source code
findings.description: DB_USER and DB_PASS hardcoded as static final constants in source. Credentials committed to version control.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code — deployment-blocking security failure. Credentials in git history permanently.
findings.recommendation: Rotate exposed credentials immediately. Move all secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Entire runtime stack EOL — no patching or vulnerability scanning
findings.description: RHEL 6, JBoss AS 5.1, Java 6 all end-of-life. No patching available, no vulnerability scanning.
findings.gap: Entire runtime stack EOL with no security patches. No vulnerability scanning.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported runtime. Implement ECR image scanning and AWS Inspector.

findings.title: No application security pipeline — known vulnerabilities undetected
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists; no SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. SQL injection and XXE vulnerabilities persist undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning. Known vulnerabilities (SQL injection, XXE) persist.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST and dependency scanning when establishing CI/CD. Add blocking gates on critical findings.

findings.title: No distributed tracing instrumentation
findings.description: No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, or any tracing. Failures returned as raw exception text with no correlation.
findings.gap: No tracing capability. Request flows cannot be tracked or debugged.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK or X-Ray. Propagate trace IDs in SOAP headers.

findings.title: No SLO definitions or monitoring
findings.description: No SLOs, no CloudWatch alarms, no latency tracking, no error rate monitoring.
findings.gap: No SLOs. Cannot measure whether service meets partner expectations.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for availability and latency. Implement CloudWatch metrics and alarms.

findings.title: No business metrics published
findings.description: No custom business metrics. No tracking of orders processed, values, or partner activity.
findings.gap: No business metric visibility. Cannot measure business value delivery.
findings.recommendation: Publish CloudWatch metrics: orders_submitted, order_amount, errors_by_type, partner_activity.

findings.title: No alerting configured — failures go undetected
findings.description: No alerting, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration. Failures only detected when partners report them.
findings.gap: No alerting of any kind. Service failures go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on error rate and latency. Integrate with SNS/PagerDuty.

findings.title: Zero automated tests — no regression protection
findings.description: No unit tests, integration tests, or contract tests. Partner onboarding is manual SOAP-UI session.
findings.gap: No automated testing. No regression protection during changes.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests for SOAP contract and unit tests for business logic. Run in CI pipeline.

findings.title: No observability ownership — monitoring entirely absent
findings.description: No dashboards, alarms, CODEOWNERS, or SLO definitions with team attribution. Service has no monitoring infrastructure.
findings.gap: No observability ownership. Monitoring is entirely absent.
findings.recommendation: Establish service-level dashboards, assign alarm owners, create CODEOWNERS for monitoring config.
